components.gap: Missing parts of the 1950 first-edition presentation: (a) Construct Carnap's infinite system (D56-1): m and c defined as limits over the fitting finite systems, with the countable named domain and effectivity hypotheses stated; for the monadic language prove that the m* limit exists for every general sentence, give the effective reduction of a general sentence to a nongeneral sentence with the same m*-value, and prove 110A (5) that a purely general sentence has m* equal to 0 or 1 (1950 sec.110A pp.566-567); then prove the T81-2a logical transfer of the finite comparative adequacy theorem to arbitrary general sentences of that infinite language with its limit-existence conditions. (b) Present the 1950 sec.41 interpretations of probability_1 (evidential support, fair betting quotient, estimate of relative frequency, pp.162-175), which the explication/two-concepts presentation (carnap-logical lines 5-37) omits. (c) Present and prove the 1950 sec.95 binomial law and the sec.96 parts of Bernoulli's theorem for symmetric c-functions with their restricting conditions (cited by 110B p.567); the reader gives only the hypergeometric law and its fixed-sample limit (carnap-logical lines 286-311). (d) State the 1950 sec.110I variety-of-instances requirement and Carnap's assertion that c* satisfies it (pp.575-576) in its own terms; it is now only named in a boundary (carnap-logical lines 570-573).

Written proofs exist for every displayed finite theorem, but the proofs and prerequisite constructions owed by the presentation are missing for: the L_infinity limit definitions and their countable-domain/effectivity hypotheses, existence and effective computation of m* for general sentences, 110A (5), the T81-2a transfer for general sentences, the sec.95 binomial law and the sec.96 Bernoulli theorem parts, and the 110I variety-of-instances claim.

Give an explicit source-to-host notation and statement bridge for every reconstructed 1950 item (Carnap's L_N/L_infinity, state description, Str, Q-numbers, kappa, w, r, in/pr, D/T numbering, formula numbers (1)-(17)) and, item by item, mark which proofs Carnap printed (e.g. the 110A proof of (1)(a)(b), p.564) versus independent reconstructions, preserving the original proof route where one is printed. Bridge items for the missing presentation parts (infinite system, sec.41, secs.95-96, 110I) are also absent.

blocked.detail: 1950 sec.110A p.566 asserts without proof ('It can be shown') that the m* limit exists and is effectively computable for every general sentence of L_infinity; for languages with relations no held source supplies a proof, so this is an exact unproved step (the monadic case is a writable gap).

MP-0 asks to construct the comparative vindication of c* and the full quantitative-language confirmation function; the 1950 source itself defers both (110A p.563, vol. II; secs.98-100 'future task'). Whether a host construction beyond the 1950 source is owed needs a user decision.
The proof of the 110I variety-of-instances assertion is delegated by Carnap to [Inductive] sec.15 = Carnap 1945, 'On Inductive Logic', Philosophy of Science 12, sec.15; not held.
